newsitem.title: USA: Kennecott cancels September smelter outtage.
newsitem.headline: Kennecott cancels September smelter outtage.

text.p: Kennecott Copper, the Utah-based copper producing subsidiary of RTZ Corp Plc, said there will be no shutdown at its new Garfield smelter in September.

"We do not have another planned shutdown scheduled," a Kennecott spokeswoman said. In April there was an unplanned 22-day shutdown at the smelter to complete repairs and install a replacement heat recovery system.
The smelter was also shutdown in September last year because of an explosion caused by water leaking into hot metal.
Kennecott officials had hoped the smelter would reach full capacity by the end of June this year.
Due to the problems, Kennecott also brought forward to April maintenance work that had been previously planned for September, thereby shortening the expected September shutdown to five days.

"We are making progress. The flash smelting furnace we expect to be at full capacity at the end of 1996, and the converting furnace being at full capacity by the first quarter of 1997," Kennecott's spokeswoman said.
She was unable to say what was the current production rate at the 310,00 short ton per year smelter.
Meanwhile labor talks at the smelter continue. Negotiations focus on local issues before moving onto pay, Kennecott said.
No date has been set for talks about the economic package.
The present labor agreement expires on September 30.
